title: Lucky Seven 3 New York
own_credit: Pictures from Wikimedia Commons, credited above

lines.speaker: CHAP
lines.visual: card:Chapter Three · New York|Joseph C. Yates · Columbia and Cornell's state

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Albany, New York. The fall of 1821. Delegates from across the state write a new constitution. And in one document they do two things at once.
lines.caption: Albany, New York. The fall of 1821. Delegates from across the state write a new constitution. And in one document they do two things at once.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: They throw open the polls to working white men by removing the property requirement. And for Black men, they keep a property requirement so steep that it shuts out nearly all of them.
lines.caption: They throw open the polls to working white men by removing the property requirement. And for Black men, they keep a property requirement so steep that it shuts out nearly all of them.
lines.visual: card:New York's constitution, 1821|Property test dropped for white men, kept for Black men

lines.speaker: CO
lines.say: Lions, good evening from Morningside Heights. And yes, one of the men arguing for Black suffrage at that convention was Peter Augustus Jay, a Columbia man. He lost.
lines.caption: Lions, good evening from Morningside Heights. And yes, one of the men arguing for Black suffrage at that convention was Peter Augustus Jay, a Columbia man. He lost.

lines.speaker: G
lines.say: Wait. They opened the door and closed it in the same breath?
lines.caption: Wait. They opened the door and closed it in the same breath?

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Same breath, Gary. The voters ratified it in January 1822. And that November, those voters elected a new governor. Joseph C. Yates. Number seven.
lines.caption: Same breath, Gary. The voters ratified it in January 1822. And that November, those voters elected a new governor. Joseph C. Yates. Number seven.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Joseph Christopher Yates was born in Schenectady on November 9th, 1768, and he died there in 1837. He is the only governor of New York born in Schenectady County.
lines.caption: Joseph Christopher Yates was born in Schenectady on November 9th, 1768, and he died there in 1837. He is the only governor of New York born in Schenectady County.
lines.visual: card:Fact 1 of 7|Born in Schenectady, 1768 · the only NY governor born in Schenectady County

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: He did not go to college. He read law with an established firm. In a state run by Columbia men and their friends, that made him something of an outsider.
lines.caption: He did not go to college. He read law with an established firm. In a state run by Columbia men and their friends, that made him something of an outsider.

lines.speaker: CR
lines.say: Big Red, Ithaca is gorges tonight. And for the record, Cornell wouldn't exist for another forty-some years. Yates had no Ivy to skip.
lines.caption: Big Red, Ithaca is gorges tonight. And for the record, Cornell wouldn't exist for another forty-some years. Yates had no Ivy to skip.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: In 1798 he became mayor of Schenectady. He held the job through twelve one-year terms. And here's the thing. He was appointed to every one of them. Nobody voted him in.
lines.caption: In 1798 he became mayor of Schenectady. He held the job through twelve one-year terms. And here's the thing. He was appointed to every one of them. Nobody voted him in.
lines.visual: card:Fact 2 of 7|Mayor of Schenectady from 1798, appointed to twelve one-year terms

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: He helped found Union College in 1795, as one of its first trustees. He went to the state senate in 1805, and in 1808 he became a justice of the New York Supreme Court.
lines.caption: He helped found Union College in 1795, as one of its first trustees. He went to the state senate in 1805, and in 1808 he became a justice of the New York Supreme Court.

lines.speaker: G
lines.say: Twelve terms without one vote. I'd like that deal for my parking spot.
lines.caption: Twelve terms without one vote. I'd like that deal for my parking spot.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: The count in New York is easy once you know the rule. The state lists each governor once, no matter how many times they served. George Clinton is number one. DeWitt Clinton, his nephew, is number six. Then Yates is seven.
lines.caption: The count in New York is easy once you know the rule. The state lists each governor once, no matter how many times they served. George Clinton is number one. DeWitt Clinton, his nephew, is number six. Then Yates is seven.
lines.visual: card:Fact 3 of 7|New York counts each governor once · Yates is No. 7

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Count the comebacks separately, and the list shifts. George Clinton's return in 1801 pushes everybody down a slot, and DeWitt Clinton lands at seven instead of Yates.
lines.caption: Count the comebacks separately, and the list shifts. George Clinton's return in 1801 pushes everybody down a slot, and DeWitt Clinton lands at seven instead of Yates.

lines.speaker: CO
lines.say: DeWitt Clinton was in the first class to graduate under the name Columbia College. If anyone deserves a recount, darling, it's him.
lines.caption: DeWitt Clinton was in the first class to graduate under the name Columbia College. If anyone deserves a recount, darling, it's him.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Yates was sworn in on January 1st, 1823, for a two-year term. He is sandwiched between DeWitt Clinton's two runs as governor. Clinton came before him, and Clinton came right after him.
lines.caption: Yates was sworn in on January 1st, 1823, for a two-year term. He is sandwiched between DeWitt Clinton's two runs as governor. Clinton came before him, and Clinton came right after him.
lines.visual: card:Fact 4 of 7|Governor January 1, 1823 to December 31, 1824 · between DeWitt Clinton's two terms

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: These were the canal years. Clinton had sold the state on the Erie Canal, which critics called Clinton's Ditch. It ran from the Hudson to Lake Erie. It was dug with shovels, wheelbarrows and animal power, and many of the laborers were Irish immigrants.
lines.caption: These were the canal years. Clinton had sold the state on the Erie Canal, which critics called Clinton's Ditch. It ran from the Hudson to Lake Erie. It was dug with shovels, wheelbarrows and animal power, and many of the laborers were Irish immigrants.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: In April 1824, the Bucktail majority in the legislature, Yates's own side, voted to throw Clinton off the canal commission. The backlash was enormous. Clinton ran for governor that fall and won.
lines.caption: In April 1824, the Bucktail majority in the legislature, Yates's own side, voted to throw Clinton off the canal commission. The backlash was enormous. Clinton ran for governor that fall and won.

lines.speaker: G
lines.say: So the guy who replaced Clinton got replaced by Clinton.
lines.caption: So the guy who replaced Clinton got replaced by Clinton.

lines.speaker: CO
lines.say: New York, Gary. We recycle.
lines.caption: New York, Gary. We recycle.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: And DeWitt Clinton was never a man to lose quietly. He'd already run for president once, in 1812, and won eighty-nine electoral votes against James Madison. In 1802 he fought a duel and wounded his opponent, after calling him a liar, a scoundrel and a villain.
lines.caption: And DeWitt Clinton was never a man to lose quietly. He'd already run for president once, in 1812, and won eighty-nine electoral votes against James Madison. In 1802 he fought a duel and wounded his opponent, after calling him a liar, a scoundrel and a villain.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: In 1817 he'd won the governorship in a special election with forty-three thousand votes. Tammany Hall printed ballots for another man, who got fourteen hundred. Clinton founded the New-York Historical Society. He knew how to build things, and he knew how to make enemies.
lines.caption: In 1817 he'd won the governorship in a special election with forty-three thousand votes. Tammany Hall printed ballots for another man, who got fourteen hundred. Clinton founded the New-York Historical Society. He knew how to build things, and he knew how to make enemies.
lines.visual: card:DeWitt Clinton|Governor No. 6 · ran for president in 1812 · founded the New-York Historical Society

lines.speaker: CO
lines.say: And in 1825, back in office, he rode the canal boat Seneca Chief to Buffalo, then emptied two casks of Lake Erie water into New York Harbor. Theater, darling. Pure Broadway.
lines.caption: And in 1825, back in office, he rode the canal boat Seneca Chief to Buffalo, then emptied two casks of Lake Erie water into New York Harbor. Theater, darling. Pure Broadway.

lines.speaker: G
lines.say: So Yates is the guy who had to follow that act.
lines.caption: So Yates is the guy who had to follow that act.

lines.speaker: CR
lines.say: And precede it. Poor man got Clinton on both sides. Like a sandwich with too much mustard.
lines.caption: And precede it. Poor man got Clinton on both sides. Like a sandwich with too much mustard.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: And how did Yates win in 1822? He ran almost unopposed. He got a hundred twenty-eight thousand four hundred ninety-three votes, nearly ninety-eight percent. The new electorate gave him a landslide. Just not an electorate that included most Black New Yorkers.
lines.caption: And how did Yates win in 1822? He ran almost unopposed. He got a hundred twenty-eight thousand four hundred ninety-three votes, nearly ninety-eight percent. The new electorate gave him a landslide. Just not an electorate that included most Black New Yorkers.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: And here's the twist. Joseph Yates is the governor history skips. One term, wedged between a famous man and a famous ditch. But skip him and you skip the electorate he governed, the one the 1821 deal built.
lines.caption: And here's the twist. Joseph Yates is the governor history skips. One term, wedged between a famous man and a famous ditch. But skip him and you skip the electorate he governed, the one the 1821 deal built.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Before 1821, property, not race, was the main test for voting in New York. After it, almost no Black men could vote. History calls the 1820s the age of the common man. In New York, the common man had to be white.
lines.caption: Before 1821, property, not race, was the main test for voting in New York. After it, almost no Black men could vote. History calls the 1820s the age of the common man. In New York, the common man had to be white.
lines.visual: card:Fact 5 of 7|The 1821 rules effectively disfranchised nearly all Black men in New York

lines.speaker: CR
lines.say: And the canal men? The ones who dug the thing? They don't get a county.
lines.caption: And the canal men? The ones who dug the thing? They don't get a county.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: They do not. But he did.
lines.caption: They do not. But he did.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: In February 1823 the legislature carved a new county out of Ontario County, in the Finger Lakes, and Governor Yates signed the law. They named it Yates County. There is also a Town of Yates.
lines.caption: In February 1823 the legislature carved a new county out of Ontario County, in the Finger Lakes, and Governor Yates signed the law. They named it Yates County. There is also a Town of Yates.
lines.visual: card:Fact 6 of 7|Yates County, formed 1823, is named for him · so is the Town of Yates

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Before the land sales and treaties of the late 1700s, that country was Haudenosaunee land. The Seneca lived between the Genesee River and the lakes. Then the speculators surveyed it into lots.
lines.caption: Before the land sales and treaties of the late 1700s, that country was Haudenosaunee land. The Seneca lived between the Genesee River and the lakes. Then the speculators surveyed it into lots.

lines.speaker: CR
lines.say: And from there it's a short drive east to Ithaca, where Cornell sits in Tompkins County. Named, of course, for another governor. Daniel Tompkins, number four.
lines.caption: And from there it's a short drive east to Ithaca, where Cornell sits in Tompkins County. Named, of course, for another governor. Daniel Tompkins, number four.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Yates married three times, to Ann Ellice, Maria Kane, and Elizabeth De Lancey, and had three daughters. He was president of the Schenectady Savings Bank. In 1828 he was a presidential elector.
lines.caption: Yates married three times, to Ann Ellice, Maria Kane, and Elizabeth De Lancey, and had three daughters. He was president of the Schenectady Savings Bank. In 1828 he was a presidential elector.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: And then the strangest part. He died in Schenectady on March 19th, 1837, and was buried in a family cemetery. In 1889, the records say, his remains were moved to a family mausoleum in the Bronx. But that mausoleum shows no sign that he's in it.
lines.caption: And then the strangest part. He died in Schenectady on March 19th, 1837, and was buried in a family cemetery. In 1889, the records say, his remains were moved to a family mausoleum in the Bronx. But that mausoleum shows no sign that he's in it.
lines.visual: card:Where is Joseph Yates?|Moved to a Bronx mausoleum in 1889, the record says · no sign he is there

lines.speaker: G
lines.say: They lost the governor?
lines.caption: They lost the governor?

lines.speaker: CR
lines.say: Gary, they lost him while he was alive. Losing him afterward is just consistent.
lines.caption: Gary, they lost him while he was alive. Losing him afterward is just consistent.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: John Vanderlyn painted his portrait, and the City of New York still owns it. His house still stands on Front Street, inside Schenectady's Stockade Historic District.
lines.caption: John Vanderlyn painted his portrait, and the City of New York still owns it. His house still stands on Front Street, inside Schenectady's Stockade Historic District.
lines.visual: card:Fact 7 of 7|His portrait by John Vanderlyn belongs to the City of New York

lines.speaker: CO
lines.say: Roar, Lion, roar. Goodnight.
lines.caption: Roar, Lion, roar. Goodnight.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: An open door, with a toll booth for some. Joseph C. Yates, New York's number seven.
lines.caption: An open door, with a toll booth for some. Joseph C. Yates, New York's number seven.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: New York. Keep it real.
lines.caption: New York. Keep it real.
